projects.description:

change, identify vulnerable populations, assess health system capacity to manage climate change impacts, and strengthen the evidence base for health adaptation interventions and
investments; The V&A will be gender responsive and include sex-disaggregated data that will also be mainstreamed in the HNAP; The climate change and health vulnerability and adaptation assessment

projects.name: All-hazards emergency preparedness capacities assessed, including risk mapaping, and reported as per International Health Regulations(2005)
projects.description:
COVID-19 has profoundly underscored the importance of Secretariat, Member State and partner work to further the assessment and reporting of national preparedness capacities. 
Perhaps most strikingly, the pandemic has highlighted the crucial practical implications of being able to effectively assess national preparedness capacities in order to identify and address critical gaps, document strengths and build on best practices for health security. WHO has supported Mauritius in the implementation of the IHR Monitoring and Evaluation Framework through improved methodological approach to conducting the State Party Annual Reporting (SPAR) and ensuring timely submission of the report. The MOHW has led this intervention by ensuring follow up of the gaps and developing and implementing actions to enhance the health security. WHO also supported an intra-action review following the dengue outbreak as per the IHR as well as an Early Action Review for dengue. Mauritius is also considering the next Joint External Evaluation (JEE) in a view to get a more precise view of the progress made since the last JEE.

For the period 2026-2027, the following additional activities are planned: 
Provide evidence-based guidance for implementation of specific technical areas
- Strengthening the functionality and operationalisation of the Public Health Emergency Operation Centre (PHEOC) 
- Conduct TTX, SimEx, IAR/AAR as part of the ongoing efforts of IHR Monitoring and Evaluation - 
- Conduct participatory eSPAR annually

projects.name: Development of GBV referral pathway mechanisms and SOPs to strengthen national capacity for a coordinated multisectoral approach to prevent and respond to gender-based violence and harmful practices, to change discriminatory social norms, and to promote gender equality.
projects.description:
The GBV landscape in Mauritius is complex, shaped by socio-cultural norms, economic disparities, and legal frameworks. While the country has made strides in addressing GBV through legislation, policy development, and service provision, persistent challenges remain. These include underreporting of GBV cases, limited access to comprehensive services for survivors, and the need for increased awareness and prevention efforts.
UNFPA in Mauritius is actively engaged in addressing GBV through collaboration with diverse stakeholders from the oublic sector, the private sector and civil society. UNFPA supports the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family Welfare (MGEFW) to enhance GBV coordination and response. This includes technical support for Service SOPs and referrals for survivors, aligning with the UN Essential Services Package for Women and Girls Victims of Violence, with a broad objective to strengthen the national understanding of and response to GBV. Builing on a series of stakeholder consultations and workshops in 2023, in 2024, UNFPA contracted a national consultant to work on an Essential Service Package for Women and Girls Victims of Violence in Mauritius, aligning national legislation and policies of the Republic of Mauritius. The national consultant is supported by an international expert and this project aims to 
1. Ensure technical coherence in the inception phase of the development of a National GBV Executive Package.
2. Conduct tailored workshops and training sessions on GBV and the Essential Services Package for sectoral national partners, including line Ministries

projects.name: Policy and regulatory Frameworks for the development of the Ocean Renewable Energy in Mauritius are reviewed and are gender responsive
projects.description: Mauritius is seeking to reduce its reliance on fossil fuels by increasing its renewable energy share from 40% to 60% by 2030, with a focus on ocean renewable energy technologies, such as offshore wind. In 2023, a feasibility study, led by UNEP through the Technical University of Denmark Wind Department (DTU Wind), assessed the potential for offshore wind in Mauritius, identifying two suitable sites located 112 km² off the north coast. Site A for bottom-fixed foundations and Site B for floating turbines. Both sites showed promising energy production estimates with capacity factors of 40% for Site A and 42% for Site B, indicating competitive performance globally. The study estimated competitive energy production and costs, with Site A's Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) ranging from €89-121 per MWh and Site B's LCOE at €151-198 per MWh. A conceptual design for a 100 MW offshore wind farm at site A, featuring 11 MW turbines and monopile foundations, was also proposed, with cost reduction strategies that could lower LCOE to €67.5 per MWh. Further research and data collection are needed to refine the designs and validate assumptions for advancing offshore wind development in Mauritius.

projects.name: Development of comprehensive post-abortion care services guidelines, SOPs and policy/regulatory proposals to strengthen national capacity to ensure access to quality SRH care services without discrimination.
projects.description:
In 2024, the Ministry of Health and Wellness released the findings of its abortion, conducted in collaboration with the World Health Organisation in Mauritius. One of the survey’s recommendations is that all women shall receive free post abortion care, as part of obstetric emergency care, irrespective of the nature of their abortions. UNFPA advocated with the Ministry of Health and Wellness that comprehensive post abortion care is implemented through the use of protocols and guidelines, which would ensure that women are informed and supported adequately in their sexual and reproductive health and rights.

UNFPA convened a number of stakeholder meetings and further organised a 4-day workshop on 10-13 Dec 2024 on the development of Comprehensive Abortion Care Services Guidelines, Policy/ Regulatory Proposals and SOPs with key stakeholders, with technical support from WHO Mauritius. The workshop welcomed 40 participants from different institutions and Ministries, CSOs and Health Professional Associations. The participants developed their understanding of the reproductive and maternal health landscape in the East and Southern Africa region and the national context. They discussed the national legal framework and the key principles/considerations for policy/guidelines on comprehensive abortion care services in Mauritius. The workshop ended with a collective raoadmap of actions for the development of the package of services and policy/ regulatory frameworks on comprehensive abortion care.

projects.description:
While the annual monitoring of the HSSP 2020-24 was conducted internally within MOHW, and the fact that no Mid Term Review of the HSSP was conducted by the expiry date, WHO support was towards a review of Implementation Arrangements for HSSP 2020–2024. The review of the implementation arrangements for the Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP) 2020–2024 was done in December 20024 with a view to informing the development of improved mechanisms for the new HSSP. Also, the findings would guide the design of more effective arrangements to enhance the execution and performance of the upcoming strategy.

Focus of the Review
- Assess the dissemination and utilization of the HSSP 2020–2024 by stakeholders, identifying effectiveness, challenges, and enabling factors.
- Evaluate the performance of thematic working groups in supporting HSSP implementation, focusing on effectiveness, efficiency, challenges, and enablers.
- Examine the role of the Health Economics Unit (HEU) within the Ministry of Health and Wellness (MOHW) in preparing performance reports on HSSP implementation.
- Provide actionable recommendations to improve implementation and performance reporting for the new HSSP.
The review also focused on the implementation arrangements for the Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP) 2020–2024 
Furthermore, two landmark consultations were convened:
2. Workshop on the Validation of Situational Analysis for Development of HSSP 2025-2030
3. Workshops to Support Finalization of the HSSP 2025–2030. More specifically, the goals are to sensitise the leadership of  MOHW)with the contents of the draft situational analysis, glean  inputs from MOHW leadership to ensure the draft HSSP appropriately reflects national priorities and addresses the country’s health needs, and secure endorsement of the draft HSSP 2025–2030 from MOHW leadership.

projects.name: Development of the National Employment Policy in a gender sensitive and disability inclusive manner
projects.description:
The National Employment Policy (NEP) 2024-2028 for Mauritius is consistent with the new generation of National Employment Policies (NEP 2.0)1 and sets out a comprehensive framework designed to address key challenges and opportunities in the country's labour market. The adoption of the NEP lays the foundation for the ratification of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) Convention No. 122 on Employment Policy. It aligns with the objectives of Convention No. 122 by demonstrating Mauritius’ commitment to promoting full and productive employment, addressing labour market challenges, fostering decent work opportunities social progress, human rights and human dignity. Another fundamental element of the NEP is its alignment with national development strategies. By integrating with overarching national development agendas, the NEP ensures a cohesive approach towards achieving inclusive development. Furthermore, the NEP derives its policies and recommendations from detailed sectoral plans. This strategic alignment allows for a tailored approach to address specific labour market challenges within different sectors of the economy. A mixed methodological approach is adopted with the use of both quantitative and qualitative data and methods. Secondary data was collected from different surveys carried out by Statistics Mauritius and from the Ministry of Labour, Human Resource Development and Training. Social dialogue played a crucial role in shaping the NEP, with continuous consultations held with stakeholders throughout the formulation process. A total of 85 indepth interviews were conducted with representatives from ministries, the private 
 sector, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), trade unions, academia, public and private training institutions, and international organisations. These interviews provided a comprehensive understanding of diverse perspectives, needs, and expectations of the current labour market situation. The skills and employment requirements in emerging sectors were also discussed. This inclusive approach, driven by data and stakeholders’ inputs, ensured a 
 comprehensive formulation of the NEP. The vision of the NEP is to achieve decent, productive and freely chosen employment for all
people of the Republic of Mauritius to improve their livelihoods and dignity.
The NEP prioritises 4 policy priorities:
1 -Stimulate Employment Growth in Emerging and Sunset Sectors
2 - Address Education and Skills Mismatch and Labour Shortage
3 - Strengthen Labour Market Policies and Institutions
4 - Promote Quality Employment: Decent Work and Social Inclusion

This partnership includes the development of adolescent and youth policies, providing youth friendly services, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) with systems strengthening approach, providing essential life- skills to adolescents and strengthening evidence on adolescents and ending violence against women and girls.

To leave no one behind, UNFPA is working with the Ministry of Health and Wellness to support empowerment of adolescents and young people (girls and boys) including vulnerable groups and key population groups to receive the skills and capabilities to make informed choices about their sexual and reproductive health and right, and well-being through the development and implementation of an out-of-school CSE curriculum for adolescents and young people, communities and key population groups that are not in schools, colleges or any training institutes. This curriculum will be implemented in Mauritius and Rodrigues with selected target groups.
A series of consultative meetings with different stakeholders in the CSE sphere as below
1) a half-day consultation workshop with 25 youths and adolescents aged between 14-19 from marginalised communities, to understand and gather information on their needs to adapt the development of the curriculum;
2) a 3-day consultation workshop with 40 technical officers, health officers, youth officers from Ministry of Health, Ministry of Youth, Ministry of Education and representatives from NGOs to build a common understanding of comprehensive sexuality education principles and to build on their distinct experiences in delivering CSE with out-of-school young people for a more adapted CSE curriculum for out-of-school adolescents and youths.
3) a 1-day consultative workshop with 15 young people (in and out of school) aged between 16 and 20, 10 parents, and NGOs working with young people on CSE to get a better understanding on the landscape and how services can be better delivered to young people.

projects.name: Technical Assistance in the drafting of the Domestic Abuse Bill to incorpate international recommendations and align Mauritius to its international commitments and engagements to effectively and comprehensively address GBV in an inclusive manner.
projects.description:
UNFPA provided techical expertise and input into the draft of the Domestic Abuse Bill, ensuring coherence to international recommendations as related to the national context and legal framework. Consequently, the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family Welfare, with support from UNFPA, convened stakeholders to a 3-day consultation workshop to review and dicuss the draft Domestic Abuse Bill.

THe 3-day consultation marked a pivotal moment in Mauritius's collective efforts to create a society where every individual is safe and respected within their own home. The draft document represents a significant milestone in the journey towards ending gender-based violence  providing a basis for a basis for a comprehensive legal framework that addresses the specific needs and vulnerabilities of victims and survivors - in its majority women and girls.

At the heart of the Domestic Abuse Bill is the recognition of domestic violence as a violation of fundamental human rights. Every individual has the right to live free from fear, violence, and discrimination, and this legislation sends a powerful message that domestic violence is unacceptable and will not be tolerated. By incorporating international benchmarks, best practices and recommendations, the bill intends to intends to set a high standard for the protection of victims' rights and the promotion of gender equality.

Quality and gender-responsive legislation and policies are critical grounds for progress. The draft Domestic Abuse Bill will fulfil its transformative potential when it is accompanied by adequate policies, strategic frameworks and budgetary allocations from relevant sectors, with clear guidelines for law enforcement agencies, health and social service providers, and other stakeholders on how to respond to cases of domestic violence in a sensitive and victim-centred  manner, including including mechanisms for coordination and accountability.

WHO shared best practices from other countries and international guidelines on regulation of food labelling to promote food safety and healthy eating in the population.  These new regulations will address unhealthy diets which is one of the main risk factors for Non-communicable Diseases and obesity in particular.  As regards to nutrient profiling, work has started with the adaptation of existing data collection tool for data collection.  WHO has already built capacity of two key local technical persons on the AFRO nutrient profiling model which will help in the adaption of the national nutrient profiling to restrict the marketing of unhealthy food to children. projects.name: Develop and implement gender sensitive roadmap to reduce obesity
projects.description:
Mauritius with the support of the World Health Organization conducted three-day multisectoral consultative roundtable in April 2024 with participation of cross-section of stakeholders from government, the private sector, civil society and academia to come up with concrete actions to combat the obesity epidemic which affects 36.2% of the population. Using an evidence-based approach, the Obesity Roadmap prescribes a broad range of policy tools – political, fiscal and legal - aimed at tackling the obesogenic environment which encourages unhealthy lifestyles. The Mauritius Acceleration Plan to Stop Obesity 2024-2030 will address obesity which represents a significant public health burden in a country where NCDs account for 80% of the disease burden and 85% of mortalities.  Factors addressed in the Roadmap include the marketing of unhealthy foods and beverages, access to affordable and sustainable alternatives, fiscal policies, food labelling, early food environments, public food procurement, physical activity, health service delivery, public education and awareness, and country specific solutions.  the three major objectives of the Roadmap are as follows:(i) to reduce the prevalence of insufficient physical activity by 8% (57.6% to 49.6%) in children and adolescents (74.8% to 66.8%) from 2021 to 2030; (ii)to decrease consumption of unhealthy and ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages; and (iii) to increase coverage of obesity clinics to 50% through primary health centres and community based program to provide obesity prevention and management services.

The Roadmap will be implemented through a set of 5 priority actions and interventions:
•	Priority 1:Integrate obesity prevention and management in primary healthcare services and community outreach services.
•	Priority 2: Promote and create enabling environments to facilitate physical activity appropriate for all ages in different settings. 
•	Priority 3: Restrict the marketing of unhealthy, ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages.
•	Priority 4: Conduct behaviour change communication campaigns related to healthy diets, physical activity, and demand for health services.
•	Priority 5: Increase local agricultural production and accessibility to healthy foods to ensure availability and affordability of safe and quality agricultural products.  

The implementation of the specific activities under the five priorities as delineated in the Roadmap will further strengthen the interventions already in place through a multi-sectoral and coordinated approach to achieve the goal of reducing the obesity prevalence by 5% by 2030.  

Under Priority 1 and Priority 4 of the Obesity Roadmap, WHO provided technical support to conduct training of trainers and roll out of child growth assessment over a five-day intensive training.  The training empowered 90 health workers (Mauritius and Rodrigues) on appropriate child growth monitoring to enable the detection of wasting and stunting among children.  25 Health workers were empowered as trainers including 10 facilitators for training roll out across the five health regions in Mauritius.  The training of trainers further contributed to in-country capacity building (pool of trainers and facilitators) .  In the same vein, an assessment of the national nutrition information system was conducted in view of strengthening the national nutrition surveillance system in the Republic of Mauritius.  The findings of the assessment will help in standardizing and normalizing nutrition data for informed evidence-based decisions on national policies and improved nutrition programmes outcomes. Additionally, it will help to the country to report and monitor the global nutrition targets .

Under Priority 3, WHO has contributed to capacity building of key technical persons at the level of the Ministry of Health and Wellness and the Ministry of Finance on Sugar Sweetened Beverages (SSB) Taxation  during a global meeting with 14 front runner countries and others.  The Mauritian Health and Finance experts learned from other countries on SSB as well as shared Mauritius' experiences on SSB taxation.

Further, under Priority 4, WHO supported the roll out of the Behavioural Insights training in Mauritius and Rodrigues.  Some 75 multi-sectoral stakeholders (Mauritius and Rodrigues) were trained on the principles, use and application of  Behavioural insights to improve communications to tackle NCDs and risk factors; communicable diseases (dengue, chikungunya,etc) and other health issues.  Rodrigues island have prioritized a list of programmes/projects that would need further support for application of behavioural sights.

FAO:

1. Developed FSBDGs (national, evidence-based framework for healthy diets)
2. Messaging and materials developed and tested
3. Dissemination of campaign & creation of a national movement
4. Monitoring and evaluation of the campaign

projects.name: Technical support to the government to implement the Action plan of the Skills Mobility Framework for Mauritius, adopted in October 2023
projects.description:
Mauritius is well set to move the green agenda forward. Several initiatives undertaken across different ministries and relevant stakeholders to transition along a greener pathway illustrates the vision of the country to increase its resilience to climate and environmental change impacts and the transition toward a green economy. Mauritius is party to the Paris Agreement and therefore has submitted its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), which was updated in 2021, to indicate the targets set for reducing GHG emissions. In developing its NDC, ‘Mauritius recognizes the impacts of the measures taken in response to climate change mitigation and adaptation, and takes into account a just transition of the workforce and the creation of quality jobs in accordance with nationally defined development priorities, with a focus on green recovery and growth.’ 
Under the United Nations – Partnership for Action on Green Economy (UN-PAGE), over the last decade, studies and reports propose recommendations to support Mauritius to transition towards a more sustainable development path. The PAGE Mauritius Sustainability Plan: Country Programme Narrative summarizes the outcomes of the activities conducted under the programme. 
At the legislative level, a Climate Change Bill 2020 was enacted spelling out the legal framework to make Mauritius a climate change resilient and low emission country. Under this law, an Inter-Ministerial Council on Climate Change is responsible for setting national objectives, goals and targets to be reached. One of the functions of the Council is to ensure coordination and cooperation between government departments, local authorities, and other organisations involved in climate change projects. Part III of the Act establishes a Department of Climate Change to promote adaptation and mitigation measures to address climate change across sectors. 
Inclusive greener economy for Mauritius requires enhanced, well-coordinated, systematically and well-equipped human capital and skills development system. Green jobs already exist in a number of sectors in the country, but the latest climate commitments require more accelerated actions to meet the objectives aligned in Mauritius 2030. All these green strategies, policies and recommendations will be impactful provided the country has the human capital with the appropriate skills to achieve the targets set to transition to a green economy.

projects.name: Elaboration of the Decent Work Country Programme 2024-2028 (2nd Generation)
projects.description:
The First Generation of the Mauritius Decent Work Country Programme  (MDWCP I) was signed by the national tripartite constituents on 30 November 2012. The programme was initially meant to cover the period 2012-2014. However, after a mid-term review exercise that took place in October 2014, the tripartite constituents requested additional time to implement and complete their respective remaining activities. MDWCP I was subsequently extended to 31 December 2015. Another recommendation of the Mid-Term Review  was to focus on activities that were of relevance and priority to the tripartite constituents and “ensure that these are in tune with realistically achievable outputs, outcomes and constituents’ capacity”.

To ensure continued guidance and prioritisation of the International Labour Organisation’s (ILO) development support, the Republic of Mauritius embarked on the formulation of the Second Generation of the Mauritius Decent Work Country Programme (MDWCP II). The process started by the development of the country context analysis validated by the national tripartite constituents. The report gathered evidence on the work of the ILO as well as the constituents and other partners on employment and labour issues prevailing in the country and provided a strategic description of the main labour and social issues as well as national policies pertaining to the Republic of Mauritius in the year 2024.

projects.name: Technical assistance to strengthen the adolescent health services, with a special focus on young girls
projects.description:
WHO supported the MOHW to develop the National strategy for adolescent health 2024-2029. Adolescence is a critical period of growth and development, marked by physical, emotional, and social changes. 
The Objectives of the National Strategy for Adolescent health 2024-2029 are multi-folds: 
1.	Promote Health Education:
o	Equip adolescents with knowledge about physical, mental, and reproductive health.
o	Foster informed decision-making and resilience.
2.	Enhance Access to Services:
o	Provide age-appropriate, accessible, and confidential health services.
o	Ensure equitable access to healthcare, especially for marginalized adolescents.
3.	Prevent Risky Behaviors:
o	Reduce substance use, early pregnancies, and unsafe sexual practices.
o	Promote interventions addressing violence, injury, and mental health challenges.
4.	Strengthen Support Systems:
o	Engage families, schools, and communities in fostering a supportive environment.
o	Build partnerships with stakeholders, including non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
5.	Empower Adolescents:
o	Encourage participation in health-related decision-making.
o	Promote life skills development, leadership, and advocacy for healthy living.
6.	Address Social Determinants:
o	Tackle poverty, education gaps, and gender inequalities that influence adolescent health outcomes.
The strategy has already been approved by the cabinet on 16 August 2024 . WHO will continue to provide support to implement the recommendation of the adolescent health strategic plan.

framework.name: PEOPLE
framework.description: FOSTERING A HUMAN DEVELOPMENT APPROACH FOR AN INCLUSIVE AND THRIVING SOCIETY.

children.name: By 2028, all people in Mauritius thrive in a youth and gender responsive environment providing access to equitable and inclusive services and opportunities, within sustainable and resilient social systems.
children.description: Four areas have been identified for collaborative working to deliver transformative results that achieve impact at scale. The overall level of support provided by the UN will focus strongly on strengthening the resilience and relevance of institutions, systems and services in the health and social protection sector, education and skills sector, specific support for migrants in line with a human rights-based approach and institutional support for access to justice and improved accountability.

children.name: Social protection and health systems are better able to deliver timely, equitable and innovative services to all, especially youth, women, and migrants.
children.description:
This output is intended to provide the foundations for a human rights-based approach for inclusive human development to reinforce the resilience of the social contract rooted in human rights. Inclusion, resilience, and empowerment will be central operating principles for implementing and monitoring progress, within a systems approach. Innovative solutions to strengthen the health and social protection systems, including through digitalization of social registry and e-health, will be brought to the front. To the extent possible, measures of success for social protection and health depend on the provision - sustainable over time - of universal quality care and coverage, supported by accurate, systematically harvested, disaggregated data and analysis for decision making, with a focus on
those groups at greatest risk of being left behind. Social protection and health systems are central to reducing vulnerability and poverty and are also central to the Government’s and UN’s resilience agenda. Through the lens of resilience, greater consideration is also given to how to better prepare, cope and respond to the impact of shocks and disasters, including the financial sustainability of the social systems in times of multiple, overlapping crises, and the integration of climate adaptation into institutional mechanisms and policies. Transformation and resilience building within the social protection and health system can be expected amplified over the course of UNSDCF, as lessons are generated through implementation. Transformation will also be facilitated by digital solutions, and by access to innovative solutions and means of implementation (including technology transfer and finance), including through South-South, SIDS-to-SIDS cooperation.

children.name: More people, especially youth, women and persons living with disabilities, have access to education and vocational training that enables them to access socioeconomic opportunities.
children.description: This output is required to support not only more inclusive human development, but also as the primary means by which Mauritius will accomplish economic transformation, for the benefits of its people and natural ecosystems. Although the Mauritius education system is advanced, further reform is required at all levels to enable more people to develop the skills needed to thrive in an evolving society and a changing labour market, and for application of increasingly digital technologies to meet the needs of industry 5.0. The focus will not only include the provision of skills, but also on strengthening the enabling environment to provide decent work opportunities corresponding to the aspirations of the youth empowered with these skills. Particular focus must be placed on the aspirations and rights of young people, people with disabilities, women and migrants to ensure all participate in and benefit from Mauritius’ transition. Distance learning solutions and digital networks will also be explored and promoted for education, higher-education, vocational training and research.

children.name: Safe, regular and orderly migration for inclusive socio-economic development is promoted
children.description: There were around 35,525 migrant workers (holders of valid work permits and certificate of exemption) in Mauritius as of March 2023 and the efficient functioning of the economy depends upon a steady stream of migrants. Optimizing the positive impact of migration is important to ensure to fill a significant number of positions in the labour market, but also to maintain the solid social contract in a country and a society that was built through successive migration waves.

children.name: Strong, efficient and accountable institutions provide improved access to justice, particularly for vulnerable groups.
children.description:
This output has been designed to support the Government and sustainable development stakeholders in civil society and the private sector to continue to improve in its performance in regard to access to justice for all people without discrimination, with a focus on women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. In addition, gender inequality continues to hamper development in Mauritius
and requires further attention. Strong, efficient and accountable institutions, founded on a human rights-based approach are central to SDG 16 and underpin achievement of all of the SDGs.

children.description: Two critical areas for collaborative working have been identified in which transformative results can be achieved. In order to realize these goals, the UN will partner with the Government and private sector to enable acceleration on the various prospects for the blue, green, circular and digital economy. The United Nations will also provide support to enable transitions within the food, water and energy systems of the country. Financing frameworks, digital transformation and partnerships with the private sector will seek to accelerate attainment of the SDGs and the fulfillment of human rights for all.

children.name: Enhanced, innovation driven blue, green, circular, and digital economies that provides opportunities for all, in particular youth, women, persons living with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
children.description: The potential of Mauritius’ blue, green, circular, and digital economies is still largely untapped. Opportunities for economic diversification, a key driver of resilience to economic shocks, exist in terms of harnessing ocean-based resources in a sustainable manner, including offshore renewable energies, small-scale and high-end fisheries and sustainable aquaculture, sustainable shipping and port services, blue biotechnologies, and coastal tourism. The same is true for opportunities linked to sustainable economies activities on land, and in the digital economy, which is already growing fast and producing higher-than-average wages in Mauritius. Finally, there is a strong appetite in public and private entities to make rapid breakthrough in the circular economy, with the enabling environment now in place, and several private companies pioneering circularity, from design to waste  management. The circular economy is not only an opportunity for greening the economy, but also for enhancing resilience by lowering the dependence on external suppliers. If the right set of evidence-based policy solutions is installed and effectively implemented, including by improving the availability of data on these segments of the economy, collectively these opportunities should lead to unleashing the potential of the blue economy in Mauritius. Access to concessional finance and climate finance will be key to secure the public investments needed in infrastructure, equipment, and capacities to drive innovation in the blue economic transformation, and to crowd in domestic and foreign investments in these sectors.

children.name: Food security is enhanced for all – especially children, youth, women and other vulnerable groups – ensuring the transition of food, water and energy systems towards sustainability.
children.description: The analysis of the country’s vulnerabilities highlights the need for a strong focus on the water-energy-food-environment nexus60. As a SIDS, Mauritius is structurally vulnerable with limited arable land, water scarcity, limited economies of scale for private investment and fiscal space for public investment, thereby accelerating the impacts of climate change, and over reliance on strategic imports such as food, fuel, and inputs. Food insecurity has grown as an issue in Mauritius in recent years and was exacerbated by COVID-19 and inflation61. In parallel to food, water scarcity is another important issue62. In addition, the energy transition remains an important challenge and a top priority for the country. Mauritius’ has set ambitious targets in its NDCs of 60% of renewable energy (RE) in its electricity mix by 2030 from a current 23.9%, and an increase in energy efficiency by 10% over the same period. Moreover, the transformative power of the Water-Energy-Food-Environment nexus is huge, as this nexus lies at the heart of Mauritius structural vulnerabilities as a SIDS: over reliance on strategic imports such as food fuel and inputs, water scarcity, and high exposure to climate change and exogenous economic shocks. This output will then contribute to mitigate the country’s contribution to climate change, strengthen the resilience of the economy, advance energy transition and accelerate economic transformation.

framework.name: PLANET
framework.description: ENHANCING RESILIENCE TO THE TRIPLE PLANETARY CRISIS.

children.name: By 2028, Mauritius has integrated, gender sensitive and adapted systems for disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation that will address climate induced disasters, biodiversity loss and pollution.
children.description: In line with the UN Secretary General’s statement on the triple-planetary crisis, the UN will support the conservation, preservation and restoration of Mauritius’ precious natural resources and biodiversity, as well as adaptation to climate change and disaster risk reduction. Simultaneous efforts will be made to ensure that all forms of air, water and land pollution are reduced, and that hazardous substances and pathogens are better controlled. The UN will step up its support to enhance access to climate financing, including climate and loss and damage funds, by supporting Government entities and civil society organizations (CSOs) in building capacities and project pipelines to access funds, and advocating for more access to concessional and climate finance for middle- and high- income SIDS.

children.name: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
children.description: SIDS, by their very nature, are minor GHG emitters, yet among the countries most impacted by climate change. In Mauritius as in other countries, women and men are exposed differently to the impacts of climate change, and women headed households face greater vulnerability, and are most likely to be the most affected by prolonged droughts and other disasters. People living in Rodrigues, Agalega and the Chagos face specific constraints conditioning higher poverty rate, lower access to services and jobs, and higher vulnerability to climate change impact. Hence, improving Mauritius’ access to finance and technologies for the combined goal of mitigation of and adaptation to climate change is significant. The creation of a “Loss and Damage Fund”, announced at COP27 in Egypt, will be important, as will SIDS-to-SIDS Cooperation.

children.name: The country’s biodiversity is protected and the pollution of ecosystems is curbed, allowing natural ecosystems to thrive.
children.description: Surrounded by coral reefs, Mauritius has significant marine biodiversity. This has important implications not only for national and international ecosystems, but also for the living  conditions and livelihoods of all communities. Societies benefit enormously from ecosystem and biodiversity services and the social and economic activities derived directly from them, such as fisheries and tourism activities. Yet their depletion is inextricably linked with human activity, and climate change as noted in the output area immediately above, poses a potentially catastrophic threat to this rich natural endowment.
